items.stem: Define the term “sporopollenin”.
items.answer: The highly resistant organic material of the exine of a pollen grain.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the highly resistant organic material of the exine of a pollen grain.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about flower structure and development of gametophytes is correct?
items.answer: The exine of the pollen grain is made of sporopollenin.
items.markingKey: (d) The exine of the pollen grain is made of sporopollenin. The other statements are false. It is 8-nucleate and 7-celled. The vegetative cell is bigger; the generative cell is small and spindle shaped. The epidermis is outermost; the tapetum is innermost and nourishes pollen.
options: The embryo sac is 7-nucleate and 8-celled.
The generative cell is larger than the vegetative cell.
The tapetum is the outermost layer of the anther wall.
The exine of the pollen grain is made of sporopollenin.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a part of the ovule?
items.answer: epidermis
items.markingKey: (d) Epidermis is a wall layer of the microsporangium, not a part of the ovule.
options: micropyle
chalaza
hilum
epidermis

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The generative cell is larger than the vegetative cell.”
items.answer: The vegetative cell is bigger; the generative cell is small and spindle shaped.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The vegetative cell is bigger; the generative cell is small and spindle shaped.

items.stem: The leaf cells of onion have 16 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are present in the megaspore mother cell?
items.markingKey: (c) The megaspore mother cell is diploid (2n); n = 8, so it has 16 chromosomes.

items.stem:
A cell or structure of the flower has these features: cells have dense cytoplasm; innermost wall layer of the anther; cells generally have more than one nucleus.
(i) Identify the cell or structure. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the synergids? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The tapetum (ii) nourishes the developing pollen grains (iii) part of the egg apparatus with the egg cell; two cells at the micropylar end
items.markingKey: (i) the tapetum – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: nourishes the developing pollen grains – 1 mark. (iii) for the synergids: two cells at the micropylar end; part of the egg apparatus with the egg cell; bear the filiform apparatus – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: How many meiotic divisions are needed to produce 200 viable seeds in a flowering plant? Explain.
items.answer: 250 meiotic divisions
items.markingKey: Each seed needs one ovule, i.e. one megaspore mother cell ⇒ 200 meioses (1); each meiosis of a pollen mother cell gives 4 pollen grains, and one pollen grain fertilises one ovule ⇒ 200/4 = 50 meioses (1); total = 250.

items.stem: A cell or structure of the flower has these features: forms the pollen tube; large irregularly shaped nucleus; larger of the two cells. Identify the cell or structure. Give a reason.
items.answer: The vegetative cell of a pollen grain
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the vegetative cell of a pollen grain; 1 mark: the features forms the pollen tube; large irregularly shaped nucleus; larger of the two cells are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Describe the structure of a typical microsporangium with a labelled diagram. Explain the process of microsporogenesis.
items.answer: A transverse section shows four wall layers: epidermis, endothecium, 2–3 middle layers and the innermost tapetum, which nourishes pollen. The centre has sporogenous tissue whose cells act as pollen mother cells (2n); each undergoes meiosis to form a tetrad of four haploid microspores, which separate on dehydration and develop into pollen grains.
items.markingKey: 2 marks labelled diagram; 1 mark wall layers and functions; 2 marks microsporogenesis.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as part of the ovule or wall layer of the microsporangium: epidermis, endothecium, hilum, middle layers.
items.answer: epidermis – wall layer of the microsporangium; endothecium – wall layer of the microsporangium; hilum – part of the ovule; middle layers – wall layer of the microsporangium.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: epidermis – wall layer of the microsporangium; endothecium – wall layer of the microsporangium; hilum – part of the ovule; middle layers – wall layer of the microsporangium.

items.stem: Which of the following is a part of the pistil?
items.answer: ovary
items.markingKey: (b) Ovary is a part of the pistil; the others are not.
options: middle layers
ovary
integuments
endothecium

items.stem: What is meant by “autogamy”?
items.answer: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about pollination and pollen–pistil interaction is correct?
items.answer: Wind-pollinated flowers often have a single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed in an inflorescence.
items.markingKey: (a) Wind-pollinated flowers often have a single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed in an inflorescence. The other statements are false. Water pollination is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocots such as Vallisneria, Hydrilla and Zostera; grasses are wind pollinated. The moth lays eggs in the ovary and its larvae feed on some developing seeds. They have small, inconspicuous flowers; insect-pollinated flowers are colourful and scented.
options: Wind-pollinated flowers often have a single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed in an inflorescence.
Wind-pollinated flowers have large, colourful petals and nectar.
In Yucca the moth gets nothing in return for pollinating the flower.
Most water-pollinated plants are monocots like grasses.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a wind-pollinated plant?
items.answer: Yucca
items.markingKey: (b) Yucca is an insect-pollinated plant, not a wind-pollinated plant.
options: wheat
Yucca
grasses
rice

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Wind-pollinated flowers have large, colourful petals and nectar.”
items.answer: They have small, inconspicuous flowers; insect-pollinated flowers are colourful and scented.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: They have small, inconspicuous flowers; insect-pollinated flowers are colourful and scented.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about pollination and pollen–pistil interaction is incorrect?
items.answer: Cleistogamous flowers are always cross-pollinated.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “Cleistogamous flowers are always cross-pollinated.” Correct form: They never open, so only autogamy occurs.
options: Cleistogamous flowers are always cross-pollinated.
Pollen of wind-pollinated plants is light and non-sticky.
In Vallisneria the female flower reaches the water surface by a long stalk.
Cleistogamous flowers produce assured seed set even without pollinators.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct sequence of steps in an artificial hybridisation programme?
items.answer: selection of parents → emasculation → bagging → rebagging
items.markingKey: (c) selection of parents → emasculation → bagging → rebagging. Emasculate before dehiscence, bag, then pollinate with desired pollen and rebag.
options: bagging → emasculation → selection of parents → rebagging
bagging → emasculation → rebagging → selection of parents
selection of parents → emasculation → bagging → rebagging
rebagging → bagging → emasculation → selection of parents

items.stem:
A plant breeder in Ludhiana wants to cross a wheat variety with high yield (female parent) with one that is rust resistant.
(i) Why must she emasculate the flowers of the female parent? (1 mark)
(ii) Why are the flowers bagged? (1 mark)
(iii) What would be different if the female parent had unisexual flowers? Explain. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Wheat flowers are bisexual; anthers must be removed before dehiscence to prevent self-pollination. (ii) Bagging with butter paper prevents contamination by unwanted pollen. (iii) Emasculation is not needed; female flower buds are only bagged, dusted with the desired pollen when the stigma is receptive, and rebagged.

items.stem: Why is xenogamy considered better than autogamy? Give two outbreeding devices.
items.answer: Xenogamy brings genetically different pollen and produces variation and vigour. Outbreeding devices: pollen release and stigma receptivity not synchronised, anther and stigma at different positions, self-incompatibility, unisexual flowers (monoecy in castor/maize, dioecy in papaya).
items.markingKey: 1 mark advantage; 1 mark two devices.

items.stem: Which term describes flowers that do not open at all, so that only autogamy is possible?
items.answer: cleistogamous flowers
items.markingKey: (d) Cleistogamous flowers: flowers that do not open at all, so that only autogamy is possible.
options: emasculation
self-incompatibility
pollen–pistil interaction
cleistogamous flowers

items.stem: Which of the following is a plant with cleistogamous flowers?
items.answer: Commelina
items.markingKey: (d) Commelina is a plant with cleistogamous flowers; the others are not.
options: rice
Zostera
Yucca
Commelina

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between wind pollination and insect pollination on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A flower shows these adaptations: sticky pollen. Which mode of pollination is it adapted for – wind pollination or insect pollination? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Wind pollination: light, non-sticky pollen; well-exposed stamens; large feathery stigma. Insect pollination: large, colourful, fragrant flowers; rich in nectar; sticky pollen. (b) Insect pollination.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: insect pollination; 1 mark: “sticky pollen” is a feature of insect pollination.

items.stem: Define the term “emasculation”.
items.answer: The removal of anthers from a bisexual flower bud before the anther dehisces.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the removal of anthers from a bisexual flower bud before the anther dehisces.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of pollen–pistil interaction: tube enters ovule through micropyle, pollen lands on stigma, pistil recognises compatible pollen, tube enters a synergid. Give a reason.
items.answer: pollen lands on stigma → pistil recognises compatible pollen → tube enters ovule through micropyle → tube enters a synergid
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order pollen lands on stigma → pistil recognises compatible pollen → tube enters ovule through micropyle → tube enters a synergid; 1 mark for the reason: Guided by the filiform apparatus.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as wind-pollinated plant or plant with cleistogamous flowers: maize, wheat, Commelina, Viola (common pansy).
items.answer: maize – wind-pollinated plant; wheat – wind-pollinated plant; Commelina – plant with cleistogamous flowers; Viola (common pansy) – plant with cleistogamous flowers.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: maize – wind-pollinated plant; wheat – wind-pollinated plant; Commelina – plant with cleistogamous flowers; Viola (common pansy) – plant with cleistogamous flowers.

items.stem: What is meant by “double fertilisation”?
items.answer: The occurrence of syngamy and triple fusion in the same embryo sac.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the occurrence of syngamy and triple fusion in the same embryo sac.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as non-albuminous (exalbuminous) seed or seed with perisperm: beet, pea, black pepper, bean.
items.answer: beet – seed with perisperm; pea – non-albuminous (exalbuminous) seed; black pepper – seed with perisperm; bean – non-albuminous (exalbuminous) seed.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: beet – seed with perisperm; pea – non-albuminous (exalbuminous) seed; black pepper – seed with perisperm; bean – non-albuminous (exalbuminous) seed.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a non-albuminous (exalbuminous) seed?
items.answer: strawberry
items.markingKey: (a) Strawberry is a false fruit, not a non-albuminous (exalbuminous) seed.
options: strawberry
groundnut
bean
pea

items.stem: After fertilisation, a part of the flower develops as follows: outer becomes testa, inner becomes tegmen; form the seed coat. Which part of the ovule or flower forms it? Give a reason.
items.answer: The integuments
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the integuments; 1 mark: the features outer becomes testa, inner becomes tegmen; form the seed coat are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Give two differences between the ovary wall and the integuments.
items.answer: The ovary wall: may be dry as in groundnut and mustard; forms the pericarp (fruit wall). The integuments: harden as protective layers; outer becomes testa, inner becomes tegmen.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. the ovary wall – may be dry as in groundnut and mustard; forms the pericarp (fruit wall); the integuments – harden as protective layers; outer becomes testa, inner becomes tegmen.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about double fertilisation and post-fertilisation events is incorrect?
items.answer: In pea and groundnut the endosperm persists in the mature seed.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “In pea and groundnut the endosperm persists in the mature seed.” Correct form: They are non-albuminous; the endosperm is used up by the developing embryo.
options: In pea and groundnut the endosperm persists in the mature seed.
Endosperm development precedes embryo development.
The coconut water is free-nuclear endosperm and the white kernel is cellular endosperm.
The primary endosperm nucleus is triploid.

items.stem:
Rahul splits open a tender coconut and finds sweet water inside; a mature coconut has a thick white kernel.
(i) What does the coconut water represent? (1 mark)
(ii) What is the white kernel? (1 mark)
(iii) What is the ploidy of these tissues and how are they formed? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Free-nuclear endosperm (thousands of nuclei). (ii) Cellular endosperm. (iii) Triploid (3n); formed from the primary endosperm nucleus produced by triple fusion of a male gamete with two polar nuclei.

items.stem: Why is fertilisation in angiosperms called double fertilisation? Name the products formed.
items.answer: Two fusions occur in each embryo sac: syngamy (male gamete + egg → diploid zygote) and triple fusion (male gamete + two polar nuclei → triploid primary endosperm nucleus).
items.markingKey: 1 mark two fusions; 1 mark products with ploidy.

items.stem: Which of the following is a non-albuminous (exalbuminous) seed?
items.answer: groundnut
items.markingKey: (b) Groundnut is a non-albuminous (exalbuminous) seed; the others are not.
options: black pepper
groundnut
barley
maize

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Embryo develops before the endosperm.”
items.answer: The endosperm develops first, to nourish the embryo.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The endosperm develops first, to nourish the embryo.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about double fertilisation and post-fertilisation events is correct?
items.answer: Endosperm development precedes embryo development.
items.markingKey: (d) Endosperm development precedes embryo development. The other statements are false. The endosperm develops first, to nourish the embryo. It is triploid (two polar nuclei + one male gamete). The ovule develops into the seed; the ovary develops into the fruit.
options: The primary endosperm nucleus is diploid.
The ovule develops into the fruit.
Embryo develops before the endosperm.
Endosperm development precedes embryo development.

items.stem: After fertilisation, a part of the flower develops as follows: repeated free-nuclear divisions in coconut; triploid. Which part of the ovule or flower forms it?
items.answer: the primary endosperm cell
items.markingKey: (d) The primary endosperm cell: repeated free-nuclear divisions in coconut; triploid.
options: the zygote
the ovary wall
the integuments
the primary endosperm cell

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The primary endosperm nucleus is triploid.
Reason (R): It is formed by fusion of two polar nuclei with one male gamete.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) n + n + n = 3n.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by “triple fusion”?
items.answer: The fusion of the second male gamete with the two polar nuclei to form the primary endosperm nucleus.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the fusion of the second male gamete with the two polar nuclei to form the primary endosperm nucleus.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): After fertilisation the integuments form the fruit wall.
Reason (R): The primary endosperm nucleus is triploid.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Integuments form the seed coat; the ovary wall forms the pericarp. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by “parthenocarpy”?
items.answer: The development of fruit without fertilisation, giving seedless fruits.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the development of fruit without fertilisation, giving seedless fruits.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about apomixis, parthenocarpy and polyembryony is correct?
items.answer: Apomictic embryos are genetically identical to the parent.
items.markingKey: (a) Apomictic embryos are genetically identical to the parent. The other statements are false. Apomixis produces seeds without fertilisation. Hybrid characters segregate in the progeny, so hybrid seed must be bought every year. They are seedless as no fertilisation occurs.
options: Apomictic embryos are genetically identical to the parent.
Apomixis requires fertilisation of the egg.
Seeds of hybrids maintain hybrid characters in the next generation.
Parthenocarpic fruits contain many seeds.

items.stem: A special mode of reproduction in plants shows: fruits are seedless; seen in banana; fruit without fertilisation. Which phenomenon is it? Give a reason.
items.answer: Parthenocarpy
items.markingKey: 1 mark: parthenocarpy; 1 mark: the features fruits are seedless; seen in banana; fruit without fertilisation are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about apomixis, parthenocarpy and polyembryony is incorrect?
items.answer: Seeds of hybrids maintain hybrid characters in the next generation.
items.markingKey: (b) The incorrect statement is “Seeds of hybrids maintain hybrid characters in the next generation.” Correct form: Hybrid characters segregate in the progeny, so hybrid seed must be bought every year.
options: If hybrids are made apomictic, farmers can keep using hybrid seed year after year.
Seeds of hybrids maintain hybrid characters in the next generation.
Banana is a parthenocarpic fruit.
Apomictic embryos are genetically identical to the parent.

items.stem:
Seema notices that when she sows seeds from the orange tree in her garden at Nagpur, several seedlings come out of a single seed.
(i) Name the phenomenon. (1 mark)
(ii) From which cells do the extra embryos arise? (1 mark)
(iii) Are the seedlings genetically like the parent? Explain, and state one advantage to horticulture. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Polyembryony. (ii) Nucellar cells that protrude into the embryo sac (nucellar embryony). (iii) Yes, nucellar embryos are clones of the mother plant as they form without fertilisation; uniform, true-to-type seedlings can be raised.

items.stem: Which of the following is a parthenocarpic fruit?
items.answer: banana
items.markingKey: (a) Banana is a parthenocarpic fruit; the others are not.
options: banana
grasses (some species)
jamun (Syzygium)
mango

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Apomixis is important for the hybrid seed industry.
Reason (R): Apomictic hybrids do not show segregation of characters.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Seed can be reused.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Parthenocarpic fruits contain many seeds.”
items.answer: They are seedless as no fertilisation occurs.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: They are seedless as no fertilisation occurs.

items.stem: Give two differences between parthenocarpy and apomixis.
items.answer: Parthenocarpy: fruit without fertilisation; can be induced by growth hormones. Apomixis: embryo genetically identical to the parent; seen in some Asteraceae and grasses.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. parthenocarpy – fruit without fertilisation; can be induced by growth hormones; apomixis – embryo genetically identical to the parent; seen in some Asteraceae and grasses.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between apomixis and polyembryony on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A special mode of reproduction in plants shows: extra embryos are genetically identical to the parent. Which phenomenon is it – apomixis or polyembryony? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Apomixis: seeds without fertilisation; embryo genetically identical to the parent; seen in some Asteraceae and grasses. Polyembryony: more than one embryo in a seed; often from nucellar cells; seen in citrus and mango. (b) Polyembryony.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: polyembryony; 1 mark: “extra embryos are genetically identical to the parent” is a feature of polyembryony.

items.stem: A flower shows these adaptations: well-exposed stamens; large feathery stigma; light, non-sticky pollen. Which mode of pollination is it adapted for? Give a reason.
items.answer: Wind pollination
items.markingKey: 1 mark: wind pollination; 1 mark: the features well-exposed stamens; large feathery stigma; light, non-sticky pollen are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a parthenocarpic fruit?

items.stem: Explain the term “the filiform apparatus”.
items.answer: The special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip of the synergids that guide the pollen tube.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the special cellular thickenings at the micropylar tip of the synergids that guide the pollen tube.

items.stem:
A cell or structure of the flower has these features: two cells at the micropylar end; bear the filiform apparatus; part of the egg apparatus with the egg cell.
(i) Identify the cell or structure. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the tapetum? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The synergids (ii) guide the entry of the pollen tube (iii) cells have dense cytoplasm; cells generally have more than one nucleus
items.markingKey: (i) the synergids – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: guide the entry of the pollen tube – 1 mark. (iii) for the tapetum: innermost wall layer of the anther; cells have dense cytoplasm; cells generally have more than one nucleus – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about double fertilisation and post-fertilisation events is correct?
items.answer: The zygote develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac.
items.markingKey: (b) The zygote develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac. The other statements are false. They are non-albuminous; the endosperm is used up by the developing embryo. Integuments form the seed coat; the ovary wall forms the pericarp. The ovule develops into the seed; the ovary develops into the fruit.
options: After fertilisation the integuments form the fruit wall.
The zygote develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac.
The ovule develops into the fruit.
In pea and groundnut the endosperm persists in the mature seed.

items.stem: Give two differences between insect pollination and water pollination.
items.answer: Insect pollination: rich in nectar; flowers may be clustered into inflorescences to be conspicuous. Water pollination: long ribbon-like pollen in seagrasses; flowers at or below water surface.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. insect pollination – rich in nectar; flowers may be clustered into inflorescences to be conspicuous; water pollination – long ribbon-like pollen in seagrasses; flowers at or below water surface.

items.stem: A flower shows these adaptations: seen in Vallisneria and Zostera; flowers at or below water surface; pollen protected by a mucilaginous covering. Which mode of pollination is it adapted for? Give a reason.
items.answer: Water pollination
items.markingKey: 1 mark: water pollination; 1 mark: the features seen in Vallisneria and Zostera; flowers at or below water surface; pollen protected by a mucilaginous covering are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a parthenocarpic fruit?
items.answer: some species of Asteraceae
items.markingKey: (c) Some species of Asteraceae is a plant showing apomixis, not a parthenocarpic fruit.
options: seedless watermelon (induced)
seedless grapes (induced)
some species of Asteraceae
banana

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence in the development of the embryo sac: 4-nucleate stage, 2-nucleate stage, four megaspores, megaspore mother cell. Give a reason.
items.answer: megaspore mother cell → four megaspores → 2-nucleate stage → 4-nucleate stage
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order megaspore mother cell → four megaspores → 2-nucleate stage → 4-nucleate stage; 1 mark for the reason: One meiosis then three free-nuclear mitoses.

items.stem: Which term describes a state of inactivity in which the seed's metabolic activity slows down as it matures?
items.answer: seed dormancy
items.markingKey: (c) Seed dormancy: a state of inactivity in which the seed's metabolic activity slows down as it matures.
options: double fertilisation
perisperm
seed dormancy
the scutellum

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Geitonogamy is genetically different from autogamy.”
items.answer: The pollen comes from the same plant, so it is genetically similar to autogamy.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The pollen comes from the same plant, so it is genetically similar to autogamy.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Polyembryony means more than one seed in a fruit.
Reason (R): Polyembryony is common in citrus and mango.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: It means more than one embryo in a seed. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: After fertilisation, a part of the flower develops as follows: forms the endosperm; repeated free-nuclear divisions in coconut. Which part of the ovule or flower forms it? Give a reason.
items.answer: The primary endosperm cell
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the primary endosperm cell; 1 mark: the features forms the endosperm; repeated free-nuclear divisions in coconut are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
A flower shows these adaptations: rich in nectar; sticky pollen; large, colourful, fragrant flowers.
(i) Which mode of pollination is it adapted for? (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were water pollination? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Insect pollination (ii) flowers may be clustered into inflorescences to be conspicuous (iii) long ribbon-like pollen in seagrasses; pollen protected by a mucilaginous covering
items.markingKey: (i) insect pollination – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: flowers may be clustered into inflorescences to be conspicuous – 1 mark. (iii) for water pollination: pollen protected by a mucilaginous covering; flowers at or below water surface; long ribbon-like pollen in seagrasses – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as wall layer of the microsporangium or part of the stamen: filament, anther, tapetum, middle layers.
items.answer: filament – part of the stamen; anther – part of the stamen; tapetum – wall layer of the microsporangium; middle layers – wall layer of the microsporangium.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: filament – part of the stamen; anther – part of the stamen; tapetum – wall layer of the microsporangium; middle layers – wall layer of the microsporangium.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about flower structure and development of gametophytes is incorrect?
items.answer: Sporopollenin is easily degraded by enzymes.
items.markingKey: (c) The incorrect statement is “Sporopollenin is easily degraded by enzymes.” Correct form: Sporopollenin resists high temperature, strong acids and alkali, and no enzyme is known to degrade it.
options: The vegetative cell of a pollen grain is larger and has abundant food reserve.
The exine of the pollen grain is made of sporopollenin.
Sporopollenin is easily degraded by enzymes.
Pollen grains of many species can be stored in liquid nitrogen at −196 °C.

items.stem: Define the term “parthenocarpy”.
items.answer: The development of fruit without fertilisation, giving seedless fruits.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the development of fruit without fertilisation, giving seedless fruits.

items.stem: In onion (2n = 16), give the ploidy and the chromosome number of (i) an antipodal cell and (ii) an endosperm cell.
items.markingKey: n = 8 (½); (i) an antipodal cell: n = 8 (½ + ½); (ii) an endosperm cell: 3n = 24 (½).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Wind-pollinated flowers often have a single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed in an inflorescence.
Reason (R): In Yucca the moth gets nothing in return for pollinating the flower.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The moth lays eggs in the ovary and its larvae feed on some developing seeds.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The ovule develops into the fruit.”
items.answer: The ovule develops into the seed; the ovary develops into the fruit.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The ovule develops into the seed; the ovary develops into the fruit.

items.stem: Which of the following is a seed with perisperm?
items.answer: black pepper
items.markingKey: (c) Black pepper is a seed with perisperm; the others are not.
options: castor
bean
black pepper
strawberry

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Emasculation is needed only if the female parent bears bisexual flowers.
Reason (R): In unisexual female flowers there are no anthers to remove.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Only bagging is needed for unisexual flowers.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: What is meant by “megasporogenesis”?
items.answer: The formation of megaspores from the megaspore mother cell.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the formation of megaspores from the megaspore mother cell.

items.stem:
A cell or structure of the flower has these features: haploid; part of the embryo sac; three cells at the chalazal end.
(i) Identify the cell or structure. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the tapetum? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The antipodal cells (ii) usually degenerate (iii) innermost wall layer of the anther; nourishes the developing pollen grains
items.markingKey: (i) the antipodal cells – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: usually degenerate – 1 mark. (iii) for the tapetum: innermost wall layer of the anther; cells have dense cytoplasm; cells generally have more than one nucleus – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about double fertilisation and post-fertilisation events is correct?
items.answer: The zygote develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac.
items.markingKey: (b) The zygote develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac. The other statements are false. The endosperm develops first, to nourish the embryo. They are non-albuminous; the endosperm is used up by the developing embryo. Integuments form the seed coat; the ovary wall forms the pericarp.
options: In pea and groundnut the endosperm persists in the mature seed.
The zygote develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac.
Embryo develops before the endosperm.
After fertilisation the integuments form the fruit wall.

items.stem: Give two differences between insect pollination and wind pollination.
items.answer: Insect pollination: rich in nectar; large, colourful, fragrant flowers. Wind pollination: well-exposed stamens; single ovule in each ovary.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. insect pollination – rich in nectar; large, colourful, fragrant flowers; wind pollination – well-exposed stamens; single ovule in each ovary.
